title: Spring News Roundup: First Milestone Releases for Boot, Framework, Data, Security, Modulith, Batch
author: Michael Redlich
gist: After a 10-week release hiatus, the Spring ecosystem shipped first-milestone releases across ten projects (Boot, Framework, Data, Security, Integration, HATEOAS, Modulith, Batch, AMQP, Kafka) and patched over 90 CVEs, including a Spring Integration deserialization RCE and a Spring AMQP admin-password leak.

insights.claim: After a 10-week hiatus since the last batch of Spring ecosystem releases, the week of August 17, 2026 saw first milestone releases across ten projects simultaneously: Spring Boot, Spring Framework, Spring Data, Spring Security, Spring Integration, Spring HATEOAS, Spring Modulith, Spring Batch, Spring AMQP, and Spring for Apache Kafka.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: A synchronized major-version milestone wave (Boot 4.2, Framework 7.1, etc.) signals a coordinated Spring ecosystem release train converging toward stable releases, relevant to enterprise Java shops planning upgrade cycles and dependency compatibility windows.
insights.quote: After a 10-week hiatus since the last batch of Spring ecosystem releases, there was a flurry of activity during the week of August 17th, 2026, highlighting first milestone releases of: Spring Boot, Spring Framework, Spring Data, Spring Security, Spring Integration, Spring HATEOAS, Spring Modulith, Spring Batch, Spring AMQP and Spring for Apache Kafka.

insights.claim: Over 90 CVEs were addressed across the various Spring project releases in this cycle, with details tracked on the Spring Security Advisories page.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: A large simultaneous batch of security patches (90+ CVEs) across a framework underpinning a huge share of enterprise Java applications means IT security teams should prioritize this release cycle for patching, and it's a reminder of Spring's outsized position in enterprise software supply-chain risk.
insights.quote: In addition, over 90 CVEs were addressed across many of the Spring projects, some of which we examine here.

insights.claim: CVE-2026-59307 in Spring Integration allowed an attacker to write bytes into a message store because the addAllowedPatterns() method replaced the deserializing converter with a permit-all instance while the row mapper retained its original reference and kept using it, resulting in Java-deserialization remote code execution despite the caller believing an allow-list was enforced.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: A remote-code-execution vulnerability where a security allow-list silently failed to apply is a serious, high-severity flaw for any production system using Spring Integration's JdbcMessageStore — a concrete patch-priority item for security teams and a cautionary example of allow-list logic not matching actual enforcement.
insights.quote: a vulnerability that allows an attacker to write bytes into INT_MESSAGE.MESSAGE_CONTENT due to the addAllowedPatterns() method... replace the store's deserializing converter with a new permit-all instance, but the row mapper retains its original reference and continues to use it. This results in a Java-deserialization remote code execution despite the caller believing an allow-list is enforced.

insights.claim: CVE-2026-59271 in Spring AMQP exposed a configured RabbitMQ admin password as clear text in an exception message thrown upon failure of the management aliveness check, allowing anyone with log-read access to harvest the credential.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: A credential-leak-via-logs vulnerability is a common but serious class of security bug that can enable lateral movement in production environments; organizations using Spring AMQP with RabbitMQ should audit log retention and access controls immediately.
insights.quote: an exposure that configured admin password is embedded as clear text in the thrown exception message upon failure of the RabbitMQ management aliveness check such that anyone with log-read access can harvest it.

insights.claim: CVE-2026-47860 in Spring AMQP lets an attacker publish a 1MB message to a queue consumed by an application with message decompression enabled, crashing the consumer JVM and terminating the application, requiring manual operator intervention to purge the message.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: A denial-of-service vector triggered by a small, easily-crafted message is a low-effort/high-impact availability risk for any Spring AMQP consumer using decompression — worth flagging for ops teams running message-queue-based architectures.
insights.quote: an attacker can publish a 1MB message to a queue consumed by an application that has message decompression enabled. This may crash the consumer JVM and, as a result, the application terminates, requiring an operator to manually purge the message.

insights.claim: Spring Boot 4.2.0's first milestone adds support for the AMQP 1.0 specification with RabbitMQ features, and switches to Eclipse Jetty's GracefulHandler class (from StatisticsHandler) to coordinate graceful shutdown.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Native AMQP 1.0 support broadens Spring Boot's interoperability with messaging brokers beyond RabbitMQ's legacy protocol, a relevant compatibility signal for teams building event-driven Java services.
insights.quote: support for the AMQP 1.0 specification with features from RabbitMQ; and use of the Eclipse Jetty GracefulHandler class, rather than the StatisticsHandler class, to coordinate graceful shutdown of Jetty

insights.claim: Spring Data 2026.1.0's first milestone introduces a new RedisJsonTemplate class providing initial support for Redis JSON, alongside sub-project upgrades to Spring Data Commons 4.2.0-M1, MongoDB 5.2.0-M1, Elasticsearch 6.2.0-M1, and Neo4j 8.2.0-M1.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: New native Redis JSON support in Spring Data reduces the need for third-party libraries when using Redis as a document store within the Spring ecosystem, a modest but concrete data-layer capability expansion.
insights.quote: one new feature that introduces a new RedisJsonTemplate class that provides initial support for Redis JSON
